questions.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$, $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$, given the points $A(-1,1,1)$, $B(2,-2,1)$, $C(1,2,2)$, and $D(2,-1,4).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(2i-2j+k)-(-i+j+k) \\  & =3i-3j \\  & =⟨3,-3,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(i+2j+2k)-(-i+j+k) \\  & =2i+j+k \\  & =⟨2,1,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(2i-j+4k)-(-i+j+k) \\  & =3i-2j+3k \\  & =⟨3,-2,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|-(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & 3\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 3 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(1\cdot 3-(-2)\cdot 1)+3(2\cdot 3-3\cdot 1)+0 \\  & =15+9 \\  & =24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelpiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|24|=24.
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$, $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$, given the points $A(-2,1,1)$, $B(2,1,0)$, $C(1,-1,2)$, and $D(3,-2,-2).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(2i+j)-(-2i+j+k) \\  & =4i-k \\  & =⟨4,0,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(i-j+2k)-(-2i+j+k) \\  & =3i-2j+k \\  & =⟨3,-2,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(3i-2j-2k)-(-2i+j+k) \\  & =5i-3j-3k \\  & =⟨5,-3,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -1 \\ 3 & -2 & 1 \\ 5 & -3 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ -3 & -3\end{aligned}|-0\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -2 \\ 5 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =4((-2)\cdot (-3)-1\cdot (-3))-0-(3\cdot (-3)-5\cdot (-2)) \\  & =36-1 \\  & =35.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelpiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|35|=35.
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC}$ and $\overset{\to }{AD},$ given the points $A(8,0,5),$ $B(8,-3,3),$ $C(5,2,5),$ and $D(7,-1,4).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(8i-3j+3k)-(8i+5k) \\  & =-3j-2k \\  & =⟨0,-3,-2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(5i+2j+5k)-(8i+5k) \\  & =-3i+2j \\  & =⟨-3,2,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(7i-j+4k)-(8i+5k) \\  & =-i-j-k \\  & =⟨-1,-1,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 & -2 \\ -3 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}|-(-3)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}|+(-2)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =0+3((-3)\cdot (-1)-(-1)\cdot 0)-2((-3)\cdot (-1)-(-1)\cdot 2) \\  & =9-10 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|-1|=1.
$$

questions.problem:
Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨1,2,k⟩$, $b=⟨-3,0,4⟩$, and $c=⟨2,-1,5⟩$ are coplanar.

$k=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & k \\ -3 & 0 & 4 \\ 2 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -1 & 5\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}|+k\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(0\cdot 5-4\cdot (-1))-2((-3)\cdot 5-4\cdot 2)+k((-3)\cdot (-1)-0\cdot 2) \\  & =4-2(-15-8)+3k \\  & =50+3k\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 50+3k & =0 \\ k & =-\frac{50}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=-\frac{50}{3}.$

questions.problem:
Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨1,3,0⟩$, $b=⟨0,4,2⟩$, and $c=⟨2,k,5⟩$ are coplanar.

$k=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
a\cdot (b\times c)=|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 \\ 2 & k & 5\end{aligned}|
$$

$$
\begin{aligned} & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ k & 5\end{aligned}|-3\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}|+0\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ 2 & k\end{aligned}| \\  & =(4\cdot 5-2\cdot k)-3(0\cdot 5-2\cdot 2)=(20-2k)+12 \\  & =32-2k\end{aligned}
$$

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 32-2k & =0 \\ -2k & =-32 \\ k & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=16.$
